reviewIsolation: Fresh-context review of the dirty codex/world-aware-tools worktree. The reviewer did not implement, alter, stage, commit, merge, or push product code. The only authored file is this requested durable review receipt.
issueSummary: The refinery session delete repair gives each roster row a distinct, reachable actions menu, places the irreversible delete behind the house alert-dialog confirmation, explains exactly what is removed and preserved, and clears CONTENT only after a selected session is successfully deleted. The shared ListRow root now carries both the unnamed group required by ROW_REVEAL and floated hit-testing and the existing named group/row required by marker swaps. This fixes the observed painted-but-pointer-inert action without changing row geometry or paint, and the established chat-row kebab remains healthy.

assessment.understandability: The menu item is the conventional destructive Delete action. The confirmation title asks about this refinery session, and its description says the deletion is permanent, includes all refinery runs, and leaves the named character card unchanged. Those claims match the server verb and its integration test.
assessment.distinguishability: The icon-only trigger has a stable-first accessible name containing the character name and the visible absolute start stamp. Sessions for the same character therefore have different action names while retaining the common Session actions prefix.
assessment.pointerReachability: RowActionsMenu reveal uses the shared ROW_REVEAL hover posture. ListRow actionsFloat makes the overlaid wrapper and children pointer-inert at rest, then restores child hit testing through unnamed group-hover/group-focus-within. Adding unnamed group to the ListRow root supplies the missing selector host; the focused refinery CT reaches the trigger by real hover and completes the delete path.
assessment.keyboardReachability: ListRow renders the clickable row body and action cluster as sibling native controls in DOM order. The action trigger remains a tabbable native Button even while transparent; moving focus from the row into it activates root focus-within, which reveals the trigger, and Base UI Menu supplies keyboard opening and item navigation. The existing ListRow CT independently pins the sibling tab order and separation from the row button.
assessment.confirmationAndSettlement: The action opens the shared ConfirmDialog as an alertdialog with Cancel and destructive Delete. No mutation occurs before confirmation. onConfirm returns mutateAsync, so the dialog disables and shows loading while pending, closes on resolution, and stays open with an announced retry message on rejection. The selected-session clear runs only in the resolved continuation.
assessment.selectionAndStatus: Successful deletion of the selected row clears refinerySectionSelection, preventing CONTENT from remaining drilled into a missing session. Unselected deletion leaves the current session alone. The bus-driven mutation invalidates refinery reads and its existing error toast handles failure.
assessment.visualAndA11ySafety: The ListRow change adds selector context only; it adds no box, spacing, color, or motion class. The body remains a named native button with its metadata in aria-describedby, the action remains a separately named sibling, the coarse-pointer arm remains permanently visible, and the fine-pointer arm preserves the existing no-reflow float. No additional bare group-hover consumers were found in the ListRow implementation beyond the intended reveal, subtitle swap, and floated-action behavior; named group/row marker swaps remain unchanged.
assessment.crossSurfaceRisk: The client has three actionsFloat families: LibraryRow, CharacterCard, and ChatSummaryRow, all of which already supplied an unnamed group explicitly, plus the new refinery row. Moving that invariant to the primitive root makes the contract true for every consumer. The redundant consumer class is harmless after tailwind-variants class merging. The focused chat kebab witness passes on the repaired tree.

limitations: The refinery feature CT drives the pointer path. Exact Tab-to-trigger and Enter-to-open behavior is composed from the separately rendered ListRow sibling-tab-order contract, the native Button/Menu implementation, and the focus-within selector; this patch does not add a refinery-specific keyboard-walk assertion.

No full-app screenshot or broad design-audit suite was run. The changed shared class adds selector context without adding visual values, and the focused production-React CTs exercise the affected refinery and chat row surfaces.

The focused CT stubs tRPC at the network boundary. Server deletion ownership, run cascade, character preservation, and event emission are independently pinned by the existing delete-session integration test and were inspected in source.
